column2: Local hostname/device running the VPN service; optional enrichment field populated from collector or deployment metadata when absent in raw lines.
Emitting VPN component/service name; use 'openvpn' as the normalized program label for this log source.
VPN process identifier when available; auxiliary process context only, not the primary correlation anchor for OpenVPN text logs.

Canonical VPN event category inferred from the template (e.g., vpn_initial_packet, cert_verify, peer_info, peer_connection_initiated, virtual_ip_assigned, control_message, tls_reset, inactivity_timeout).
Primary action verb or lifecycle label for the VPN event (e.g., initiated, verified, assigned, received, sent, reset, restarted, timed_out).
Authenticated VPN identity only; extract the client CN or peer name without the appended ip:port tuple. If the raw peer prefix is user/src_ip:src_port, store only the user part here.

Primary VPN connection/session anchor derived from the OpenVPN peer prefix. Prefer user/src_ip:src_port when both identity and network tuple are present; otherwise use src_ip:src_port. This field is valid even when the raw log does not expose an explicit sid.
Remote/public client IP that connects to the VPN service; aligns with src_ip in auth, audit, dns, and Apache logs.
Remote client source port for the VPN connection; distinguishes concurrent or repeated sessions from the same src_ip and forms part of the derived session_id.
Tunnel-assigned internal VPN address for the client; distinct from src_ip and dst_ip because it represents the virtual endpoint inside the VPN overlay.
Key name from peer-reported capability or client metadata (e.g., IV_VER, IV_PLAT, IV_PROTO); preserves generic peer-info semantics without overfitting to one attribute.
Value associated with peer_info_key; supports generic parsing of client capability and version metadata.
Negotiated TLS/control-channel version when present (e.g., TLSv1.3); captures the control-plane security protocol in use.
Negotiated cipher or control/data-channel crypto suite when present; supports cryptographic-profile alignment across VPN sessions.
Message authentication/hash algorithm when explicitly logged; complements cipher_suite for security-profile analysis.
Normalized VPN control-plane message content when present (e.g., PUSH_REQUEST, PUSH_REPLY, soft reset); distinct from command because it describes protocol control behavior.
Numeric or protocol-level control status when explicitly logged; complements outcome with source-specific detail.
Inbound byte count reported in traffic or reset summaries when present; supports coarse traffic-volume comparison across sessions.
Outbound byte count reported in traffic or reset summaries when present; supports coarse traffic-volume comparison across sessions.
Inbound packet count reported in traffic or reset summaries when present; helps compare session activity at packet level.
Outbound packet count reported in traffic or reset summaries when present; helps compare session activity at packet level.
Normalized result abstraction (success/failure/timeout/restart/unknown); aligns VPN lifecycle outcomes with other log sources.
